# Crete: a shared, growing Endless level bank

**Goal:** every Endless level any device makes joins one bank on the server, up to a cap, with old levels rolled
out now and then. Any device then plays a fresh level at once instead of waiting minutes for a search or falling back
to the small bundled bank, whose few levels per grade repeat. Only levels the generator really made may enter: a
level a person drew by hand (walls that spell a word, a picture) must never reach a player.

**From:** the owner: "Once an endless level is generated by any device, it should be added to the bank up to a limit
and old levels rolled out sometimes. That gets the best of both worlds." And, as a hard requirement: "we have to be
sure it was generated and not created by a person that could do dirty things like spell bad words in the maze."

## Why

A level takes about two minutes on a phone (23 s to 4.6 min). When the search runs out of budget the run falls back
to the bundled bank (`src/endless/bank.ts`), about 28 levels a grade, and its start card says "From the level bank."
On Hard from level 5 or 6 the same maze comes back over and over.

## Proof of generation: the centre of the design

The server cannot run the solver, and replaying a line proves only that a level can be won, not where it came from.
What proves a level was generated is the fact that generation is deterministic.

**The provenance tuple.** A level's search is cut into parts (`generate.ts`'s `makePart`). Part `k` of the search
for depth `d` is a pure function of:

- the generator version (`ENDLESS_VERSION`, `src/endless/provenance.ts`);
- the run's seed, tier and grade, the depth `d` and the part `k`;
- the run state it reads: the run's last `RUN_MEMORY` levels (text, situations stored, score), which give the
  originality check its layouts and the ramp its last score, plus the run's last plain level when it is older than
  those (the ramp climbs from it);
- the campaign's layouts and the code, both fixed by the version.

Each round inside the part draws from `rngOf('endless', seed, tier, grade, depth, 'part', k, round)`. The search's
budget is the generator's own (`PART_BUDGET`); a level made under a browser spec's budget is never uploaded.

An upload carries that tuple with the level the part produced: its text, line, fewest moves, score, situations
stored, chapter and whether it hides walls.

**Verification by regeneration.** A level is verified only once two other devices have each re-run that single part
from the tuple and produced the same level, byte for byte, with the same line and numbers. That costs one part's
budget, not a whole level's search. The server hands a verifier the tuple only, never the level, so a verifier cannot
echo the answer back; the server compares what the verifier sends with what the uploader sent. A client's own claim
that it verified something counts for nothing: only the server's comparison does.

**The trusted runner.** Peers need traffic; with one player there is no second device. So a runner we run
ourselves works on the bank whatever the traffic: `.github/workflows/crete-verify.yml`, every six hours and by hand
from the Actions tab, on main's generator, over HTTPS only (never ssh or sftp, which the host's fail2ban punishes),
within one budget of 47 minutes of a 60-minute job. It does two things, in order:

1. **Verify.** `games/crete/tools/verify-bank.ts` lists up to 25 waiting levels (`trusted-list`, which gives it the
   tuple and the uploaded level), makes each again, and posts a match or a mismatch (`trusted-verify`, with what it
   made); it stops after 25 levels or 12 minutes, and a failed run only leaves levels for the next. The server still
   compares the level itself: a "match" whose level differs is a mismatch. One trusted match admits a level at once;
   peer verifications count as before. A level of another generator version is left for the players' devices.
2. **Generate.** `games/crete/tools/generate-bank.ts` spends the rest of the budget making new levels with main's
   generator, one worker thread per core as memory allows (each with a heap limit), and posts each straight into the
   served pool (`trusted-add`). The runner is our own code on our own infrastructure, so a level it made is as trusted
   as a verdict it gives. The level still goes up with its full provenance tuple, which the server checks like any
   upload's and keeps beside it, so it can be made again later.

**What the runner makes.** It first reads how full each grade is (`trusted-counts`: served and waiting counts, the
cap, and each served level's score, chapter, size and whether it hides walls) and makes the scarcest level next. The
grade is the one with the most empty room, weighted Hard 3, Medium 2, Easy 1, so Hard comes first and Medium and Easy
follow as Hard fills. Within a grade it makes plateau levels until three quarters of the grade is on the plateau,
where a run spends most of its levels, and on the plateau large boards (a long side of 21 at Hard, 19 at Medium, 17
at Easy) until half of Hard's plateau is large (a third at Medium, a quarter at Easy): those are what a run's own
search seldom finds in time, and what sends a run to the bundled bank. Each level is one part of a search
(`makePart`, `PART_BUDGET`) from a tuple of its own: a fresh seed (`ci-` and eight letters), a tier, the grade, a
depth, a part, and as run memory one plain level from the grade's bundled bank whose score sets the place, on the
plateau or on the climb. For a large board it tries seeds until the plans of the part's first three rounds are large
(the plan alone, no search), which leans the part toward a large level. A part finds a large board far less often
than a plain one, so while large boards are wanted only one plateau part in three leans large; the rest keep the
plateau filling. It never makes more than fits: a grade's room
is its cap less its served and waiting levels, a part that makes nothing gives its room back, and the server refuses
an add that would pass the cap (409 `full`), so the runner never rolls out a level a player sent. It adds no strike
and reads none. It stops starting parts when its time is spent, ends those still running, and stops altogether when
the bank's hourly share for it is spent (429) or the bank fails three times running.

It authenticates with a bearer token in the `X-Crete-Verifier` header (a custom header, since Apache in front of
PHP-FPM may drop `Authorization`). The token is `CRETE_BANK_VERIFIER_TOKEN`, the `bank-verifier` field of the item "Crete
Config" in the SIUE 1Password vault. Both the deploy and the verifier load it with
`1password/load-secrets-action` through the repository's `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` secret, as an optional load like
the studio config's: a missing item means no token, never a failed run. Disputed levels are listed to it first. The
repository is public, so the token is never committed: the deploy (`deploy.sh`, from the same item, which `deploy.yml`
loads) stages `games/crete/bank/verifier.json` holding only the token's SHA-256, and the server compares hashes.
Without the item nothing is staged and the trusted calls are refused. The action masks the token in logs, it is never
echoed in a response, and the scripts never print it. Without the item the workflow skips both steps with a notice
saying the token is not in 1Password. `bank/.htaccess` denies the whole folder to browsers.

**A device's own levels.** A level a device's own search made is trusted on that device: it is the device's own
computation. Every level its search makes is kept in local storage (`crete-endless-own-<grade>`, up to 150), and a run
on that device that finds no shared level to fit plays one of its own again, the one played longest ago, before the
bundled bank's. So a lone player always has fast levels and never meets an unchecked stranger's level. Other devices
are served a level only once it is verified.

**Two pools.** A submission waits in quarantine (`pending`), which is served only to verifiers, never to players.
With two matching verifications it moves to the served pool. A peer's mismatch disputes it: a disputed level is
never served and never handed to another peer, whatever later matches say, and waits for the trusted verifier
(below). One peer's word is no proof against the uploader, so only the trusted verifier's mismatch rejects a level
outright and counts a strike against its source; a disputed level it never reaches expires with quarantine.

**Telling devices apart without personal data.** Each install keeps a random 128-bit id in local storage
(`crete-endless-device`); the server stores only a hash of it. The server also keys each request's network on an
HMAC of its address (the kit's `clientKey` rule: an IPv6 client's /64) under a secret key that PHP makes itself,
keeps in its data folder, and replaces every three days; the key before is kept three more days, then deleted. No
address is ever stored, and once a key is gone no stored code can be traced back to one.

The rules:

- the two verifications come from two installs, neither the uploader's;
- at least one of them comes from a network other than the uploader's (one campus network may hold both
  uploader and a verifier; it may not hold all three);
- a verifier is handed a random pending level of its own version that it did not upload, has not verified and holds
  no ticket for; it cannot choose which;
- a verdict is accepted only against a ticket the server issued to that install, unexpired (an hour), once.

**Throttling.** Three strikes (trusted mismatches) in 24 hours against an install, or against a network, and the server refuses that
source's submissions for the rest of those 24 hours. Rate limits per network: 30 submissions, 20 claims, 20 verdicts,
20 reports and 120 level fetches an hour; the trusted runner's calls share 600 an hour.

**What this does and does not stop.** A hand-made level with a made-up tuple fails its first verification: the part
the tuple names makes another level, or none. To get one through, a person must also control both verifiers: two
more installs, one of them on another network, each of which must happen to be handed that pending level by the
server's random pick before any honest device is, while the server's per-network claim limits hold. With many honest
devices verifying, the odds of that fall with the size of quarantine and the number of players. We judge this
enough for a school game's maze bank: it raises a prank from "post a text" to "run a botnet that out-claims every
player", and even then the reward is one maze in a bank of thousands.

**Why nobody can steer the generator to draw.** The level text comes out of `draft` (a corridor maze carved on an odd
lattice, with a wall on every even-even corner) and `mutate` (a piece moved, a passage opened or walled), every
choice drawn from the seeded generator. A person controls only the inputs: the seed, and the run memory (which can
only veto drafts that look like an earlier level and set the score band). There is no input that places a wall. The
only way to aim at a picture is to grind seeds: run the generator on seed after seed and keep a result that happens
to look like the picture. Each try costs a whole part's search (seconds to minutes), the same as honest generation,
and the chance that a random corridor maze spells a chosen word in its walls is astronomically small: a word drawn in
walls fixes dozens of cells, and every fixed cell roughly halves the odds. Vetoes from a forged run memory cannot
help: they throw away drafts, they never draw walls.

**Allowed versions.** The server's config (`games/crete/bank/config.json`) lists the generator versions it accepts,
`accept`. A change that alters what the generator makes for the same tuple (such as the variety work) bumps
`ENDLESS_VERSION` and adds the new number to `accept`; `test/shared-version.test.ts` pins one part's output to the
version, so such a change fails the test until the version is bumped. A version taken out of `accept` is retired
whole: submissions for it are refused (403 `version`), no device is handed one of its levels to check, and its
served and pending levels are dropped from a grade's store the next time any request touches that grade, so the next
write leaves them out. No separate clean-up runs on the host. Version 1, the old repetitive 15 × 15 mazes, is
retired this way: `accept` holds version 2 alone.

## Upload

When a part's search makes a level (`from: 'made'`) at the generator's own budget, the page posts it to
`games/crete/endless-bank.php` with the tuple and the install id. It is fire and forget: one `fetch` with
`keepalive`, failures ignored, nothing retried, nothing waited on; offline, it simply fails. Seeded runs upload too:
their levels are generated like any other.

## Server checks

The server cannot solve, so it checks cheaply and refuses anything off:

- **Origin and CSRF.** The kit's score guard (`games/_kit/php/score-guard.php`): Origin or Referer on the allow list,
  double-submit CSRF (cookie `crete_bank_csrf`, header `X-Crete-CSRF`), JSON content type on every POST.
- **Rate limits** per network, as above, through the guard's `rateTake`.
- **JSON schema.** Every field typed and ranged; unknown fields refused; a body over 64 KB refused.
- **The level text.** At most 4,000 bytes. Headers only `title`, `intro`, `hearts`, `relics`, `facing`,
  `machines`, in that order; `title` and `intro` are blanked on the server; `facing` holds only the four directions,
  `machines` only `block|ball|glider|fireball` plus a direction; `hearts` and `relics` small numbers; no `pages`.
  The grid is 5 to 41 rows and columns, every row the same width, only the legal tile characters (the game's terrain,
  object and hazard characters and `P`, `M`; never `p`, a story page), exactly one `P`, at most one `M`.
  `test/shared-charset.test.ts` checks the PHP list against the game's tiles. The same rules apply to every text in
  the run memory. No free text is stored anywhere: the seed is `[a-z0-9-]{1,32}`, the line `[a-z]` only.
- **Dedupe.** A layout hash: the grid's walls as a bitmap, the smallest of its eight turns and flips, hashed. A
  submission whose layout is already served or pending is refused, so a rotated or flipped copy cannot come in twice.

Nothing from a payload is ever shown as text: players get the level's grid, line and numbers only, with title and
intro blank; the tuple is only ever sent to verifiers.

## Storage

The bank lives in `games/crete/data/` on the host, a folder the deploy makes group-writable (like `admin/data/`)
and never uploads into; PHP falls back to `/var/tmp/<account>-crete-bank` when it cannot write there (the docker
copy). `StoreDir` (`games/_kit/php/store-dir.php`) checks the folder and writes its `.htaccess` deny file. Per
grade: `served-<grade>.json` and `pending-<grade>.json`; plus `keys.json` (the network key) and the guard's rate
store, and one small `prov-<grade>-<hash>.json` per level the trusted runner added, holding its tuple, deleted once
the level has left the served pool (when the runner next reads the counts). Every change to a grade takes an
exclusive `flock` on `<grade>.lock` and writes each file whole to a new
temporary file in the same folder, then renames it over the old one, so a reader never sees half a file.

**The cap.** 1,500 served levels per grade and 300 pending. A served entry is the text with its line and numbers,
its layout hash, version, when it came in and how often it has been served: about 0.5 KB for today's 15 × 15 boards
and about 2 KB for the largest boards the variety work allows (33 × 33). At the cap a grade's file is 0.8 to 3 MB,
which PHP reads and rewrites in tens of milliseconds; `test/php/EndlessBankTest.php` measures a full store of the
largest boards and holds it under 4 MB. Pending entries carry their tuple (up to 13 earlier levels, about 4 to 26 KB
each), so quarantine is capped lower; past it the oldest pending level goes. A pending level older than three days
goes too.

## Rolling out

When a newly served level takes a grade over its cap, one served level is retired at random, weighted toward old and
often-served ones: weight = (1 + days since it came in) × (1 + times served). The newest, least-played levels are
the least likely to go, but none is safe, so the bank turns over steadily without its oldest levels all leaving at
once. Players can also retire a level: a client whose checks fail on a served level reports its layout hash, and two
reports from different installs on different networks retire it (this is also how levels a later engine change breaks leave the bank).

## Download

A request for levels names the grade and the tier and asks for up to 16; the server returns served levels of that
grade whose chapter is at most the tier, chosen at random with weight 1 / (1 + times served), and counts each as
served. The page keeps a cache per grade in local storage (up to 40 levels), tops it up when it falls under 10 (at
most once a minute), and remembers the last 300 shared levels this device took, so it never takes one twice.

**Where shared levels come in.** A run started with New Run takes shared levels; a seeded run never does (below).

- **A run's first level** comes from the shared cache when a level there fits, else from the bundled bank, as now.
- **A level the player is waiting on** (Next Level with nothing made yet): the shared cache at once, if a level fits,
  else one of the device's own; the search goes on otherwise.
- **A search that ran out of budget** answers with a shared level that fits, else one of the device's own, rather than
  the bundled bank's.
- **Levels made ahead in the background** come from the live search first, as now: devices keep generating, and
  every level they make goes up to the bank. That is the "best of both worlds": a device with time keeps feeding the
  bank, and one without plays from it at once.

A level fits when its chapter is at most the run's tier, it hides walls exactly when the run's place does, its score
falls in the band the place gives (the ramp and the hidden-wall band, `placeOf`), its layout is new against the run's
last levels (the gate's `newProblems`, and the variety work's run similarity check once it lands), it is not one this
device took before, and it passes the client checks below. Offline, the cache still serves; with an empty cache the
run falls back to live generation and the bundled bank, as before.

The start card of a shared level says "From the shared bank." where a bank level says "From the level bank."

## Client checks before playing a shared level

Cheap, on every shared level before it is played, since anyone could have uploaded junk the verifiers missed:

- the text parses, with title and intro blanked, and its chapter is at most the run's tier;
- **the line**: replaying the stored line on the game's engine wins, in exactly the stored fewest moves, with no
  catch;
- **the gate's cheap checks**: a tidy maze, no start problems, the plain walk does not win, the Minotaur is not penned
  for good, no habit player wins, and the open share of the floor is under the ceiling.

A level that fails is skipped and reported. The level's "Best" is the uploader's fewest moves. The client has proved
that many moves win; it cannot prove that no shorter line exists without a full solve, which it does not run. The
generator's own full solve made the number and both verifiers' searches reproduced it, so it is as good as a level
the device made itself. **Ruling:** no separate full-solve verification step: regeneration already re-runs that solve
on two devices.

## Determinism and seeds

**Ruling: a seed link keeps pure seeded generation.** A run started from `?seed=` or Play This Seed is seeded: it
never takes a shared level, so the same seed, tier and grade still make the same run on every device, and a link
still shares a run. New Run is not seeded: its levels may come from the shared bank, which changes over time. Its
seed still names the levels made from it, and Copy Seed Link still gives that seed's pure run, which matches the
player's run wherever the player's levels were made rather than taken from the bank. The saved run already keeps the
text of every level it holds, so continuing a run never depends on the bank.

## Verifying in the background

Any device with the game open and idle verifies: the campaign, the menus, the editor while Check is not running, and
the demo, not only players in Endless. It uses the background-generation slot's rules (`workersNow`): one worker at
most, only after the page has been quiet five seconds, never while the tab is hidden, while the solver searches (a
hint, the editor's Check, a shared level's rating), or on a low battery that is draining; outside an Endless run; and
only once Endless has nothing of its own left to make ahead, so checking others' levels and making the device's own
take turns and never run together (`mayCheck` in `src/endless/verifier.ts`). The work runs in a worker, never on the
page's thread, so it never costs a frame. Since this uses visitors' processors for the site, the game's menu has a
switch, **Help Check Endless Levels** ("Uses this device's spare time to check mazes other players made"), on by
default, and the privacy note says so. Then it claims one pending level, runs that one part in its own
Endless worker, and posts the verdict. It stops at once (ending the worker) when the page leaves those conditions,
and waits a minute between claims, and ten after the server has nothing to verify.

## Privacy

The bank stores levels. While a level waits for its checks (three days at most) it also keeps a hash of the
uploading and verifying installs' random ids and their scrambled network codes, whose key is deleted within six days.
Rate limits keep the same scrambled codes for an hour; a strike keeps the uploader's for a day, and a report the
reporter's for three days. The endpoint's CSRF cookie (`crete_bank_csrf`, seven days, HttpOnly, SameSite Strict,
scoped to the game's folder) is the game's only cookie. Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control turns the sending off
(uploads, reports and verification), as it turns off the site's visit counts; the page still plays shared levels.
`privacy.html` says so in a short section.

## Admin

**Ruling:** no admin count in this step. The admin hub lives under `admin/`, with its own login and database; adding
a reader of the game's store there adds risk for a number nobody needs yet. The served and pending counts are in the
store files.

## Tests

- **PHPUnit** (`games/crete/test/php/EndlessBankTest.php`): schema and text validation (title and intro blanked, bad
  characters, sizes, headers), rate limits, dedupe across turns and flips, quarantine never served, **a hand-edited
  level with a valid-looking tuple is never served** (a verifier's regenerated text differs: rejected, and a strike),
  two matching verifications from distinct installs and a second network admit a level, the uploader's own
  verdicts and a stranger's ticket count for nothing, strikes throttle, version accept, the cap and weighted
  roll-out, reports retire, locking under concurrent writers, the size of a full store, and the trusted calls: only
  with the token, the token never in a response or the log, one trusted match admits, a false "match" is a mismatch;
  the trusted add needs the token, is served at once with its tuple kept, refuses version 1, a duplicate and an add
  past the cap, and strikes nobody; the counts summarise each grade and forget the tuples of levels gone; and the
  shipped config retires version 1 from a live store (served and pending) and refuses its submissions.
- **node:test**: upload on make (with the tuple, never for a spec budget), taking from the shared cache (band, tier,
  hides, run likeness, never twice), the replay check, skipping and reporting a bad level, offline fallback, seeded
  runs never sharing, **a verifier rejects a text that does not match its tuple**, the version pin, the PHP
  character list against the game's tiles, the trusted verifier's script posting a mismatch for a tampered text and
  never printing its token, the trusted generator's grade priority (Hard's plateau and large boards first, never past
  the room), its tuples, its stop when its time is spent, and its quiet failures, a device's own levels played again, and checking never starting while the solver
  searches or with the setting off.
- **e2e**: a New Run takes level 1 from a shared bank seeded through the page's network layer, at once, and its
  card says "From the shared bank."

## Setup the owner does once

1. In 1Password, in the SIUE vault, keep an item titled exactly "Crete Config" with a password field named exactly
   `bank-verifier`.
2. Its value must be 32 to 128 characters of letters, digits, `-` or `_` (deploy.sh refuses anything else): let
   1Password generate 40 or more letters and digits, symbols off. Save it.
3. Run the deploy workflow once from the Actions tab (or merge anything): the deploy puts the token's hash on the
   server.
4. Optionally run crete-verify from the Actions tab to seed the bank at once: it checks the waiting levels, then
   makes new ones for the rest of its run.
